Ana (Sales): Jon, Priya reported intermittent SSE stream truncation during the customer POC. EventSource fires error and app shows `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` when parsing event.data. Happens more on mobile and over corp proxy.

Jon (SE): Can you paste the raw event fragments and SDK version?

Priya (Client Eng): From Chrome network tab (redacted):
```
data: {"req":"r1","part":"{\"text\":\"Sta"

```
Next event:
```
data: {"req":"r1","part":"rted\"}

```
They call `JSON.parse` on each data chunk which fails if the payload is split across SSE messages or splits multibyte UTF-8 chars. SDK from CDN: `@redwood/stream-sdk@1.2.3`.

Jon (SE): Likely causes: proxy adding gzip/encoding or buffering, or older SDK that doesn't preserve incomplete UTF-8 across chunks. Quick triage: 1) confirm `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and check for `content-encoding: gzip`, 2) try `curl -N` to inspect raw chunk boundaries, 3) test with `@redwood/stream-sdk@1.4.1` which has incremental buffering fixes.

Priya (Client Eng): We checked: proxy injects `content-encoding: gzip`. Disabling gzip for the stream route fixed the issue in our repro.

Jon (SE): Workarounds for the POC/demo: (a) client-side reassembly: buffer per-request parts and only JSON.parse when braces balance or id-markers indicate complete payload, (b) switch to websocket transport for the demo (`transport: 'websocket'` in SDK), (c) upgrade to SDK 1.4.1. For immediate demo I'd recommend websocket fallback (no infra change for hosted).

Ana (Sales): Any cost or security implications for websocket fallback for demo? Customer concerned about firewall and SSO.

Jon (SE): No additional cost. Websockets use wss over port 443 (TLS) so usual corporate firewalls normally allow it. For Dedicated/on-prem we may need to open ports depending on their network. Auth and audit logging still apply for websocket sessions.

deploy-bot: Released stream-fixes v2026.07.02 by @jon 2:03Z  includes SDK 1.4.1 and incremental UTF-8 preservation changes.

Priya (Client Eng): I'll send the customer two quick things: 1) how to toggle websocket fallback in their client, 2) a tiny buffer-reassembly snippet they can drop in if they can't change proxy or upgrade immediately.

Jon (SE): Also ask them for a HAR + `curl -N -v` output if they keep seeing failures so we can verify chunk boundaries and headers.

Ana (Sales): I'll coordinate with the customer for the demo fallback and share the checklist. Thanks team :thumbsup:
